newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down on political fears.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down on political fears.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished lower on Monday on investors' fears of declining law and order and political uncertainty, brokers said.
The weighted index fell 45.24 points, or 0.54 percent, at 8,269.43, off an intra-day low of 8,213.12.
Turnover was T$80.9 billion, but slowed from recent levels that exceeded T$100 billion.

Overall sentiment was dampened by a student protest in Taipei to demand resignation of Premier Lien Chan following a mass demonstration on Sunday against the government's failure to check a spate of violent crimes, brokers said.
Electronics lost 1.02 percent, despite motherboard-maker Asustek soaring by the daily seven percent limit to T$357 on its ex-bonus issue day.
Brokers had expected Asustek, which issued a stock dividend of T$15 per share, to lead other electronic shares in an upswing.
Asustek's dividend was the highest of all Taiwan listed firms' 1996 dividend issues.
"But the (ex-bonus issue) timing is not good. Investors are too cautious to chase higher prices," Hou said.
